_about: Example placeholder rules, with invented placeholder names. Copy this file to data/placeholder_rules.json (git ignores data/) and change it for your client. The tool reads data/placeholder_rules.json automatically, or the file given with --rules. Keys starting with _ are comments.

_fields.placeholders: Regular expression matched against the placeholder name (the part inside {{ }}).
_fields.includes: What the placeholder's value already contains, used in the messages.
_fields.level: Error (definitely wrong) or Check (a person should confirm).
_fields.not_before: Per language code (de, fr, pt-BR, ...): words that must not come right before the placeholder. The source_language list is used to check the source.
_fields.no_suffix_after: Language codes where letters stuck right after the placeholder are wrong (for example Turkish case endings).
_fields.replaces: Optional regular expression: a placeholder matching 'placeholders' may stand in for one matching this, with the same prefix (from {{trip.destination.name}} to {{trip.destination.toPhrase}}). This is reported as a Note, not an error.
_fields.check_source: true (default) to check the source too, reported as a Source issue for the client.
_fields.message, suffix_message, source_message: Optional wording. {word}, {placeholder} and {includes} are filled in.

rules._about: Example: {{trip.destination.toPhrase}} becomes 'to France' in English and 'nach Frankreich' in German, so a preposition or article typed before it is doubled.
Example: {{trip.destination.withArticle}} becomes 'the Netherlands', so 'the' before it is doubled.
